about: Every accepted difference of just-bash 3.6.0 from GNU bash in test/bash-oracle-cases.json (plan-bash-shell r3 §3.3), with what just-bash does instead; test/bash-oracle.test.ts fails on any other difference, or on a change in one of these. Of the 20 cases of the plan's probe, 17 file states match GNU bash's, or 16 counting exit status (D2 differs only in status). The 8 cases added here: 6 match (missing-folder through the host's wrapper, D8), amp-gt and append-then-dup are D7. The d8- cases probe D8 (astra2's CORR-BASH-D8-1): 2 match GNU bash, 8 are D8.
ipython_notes: What the frozen IPython 9.15.0 cases show, for step 6 (not differences yet: the bridge doesn't exist):

the statement form runs the command on a terminal (a pty), so its output arrives with CRLF line ends and its stderr merged into stdout; the shell has no terminal, so CRLF isn't reproduced (compare with \r\n read as \n)
the capture form merges stderr into the captured lines (capture-stderr: ["out", "err"]) and prints nothing
the capture form doesn't set _exit_code (capture, capture-status: NameError in a fresh shell); the statement form does
'$$' inside the command reaches the shell as $$ (dollar-escape), an undefined $name stays literal, and {{ }} becomes { }

cat-self-append.reason: GNU cat refuses 'input file is output file' (exit 1, f unchanged); just-bash's cat reads a snapshot, so f is doubled once and the status is 0

group-write-then-read.reason: the same file content as GNU bash; GNU cat's 'input file is output file' makes its status 1, just-bash's is 0

two-fds-offset-zero.reason: two separately opened redirections of one file: just-bash's last whole-file write wins; in bash two descriptors write at offset 0, so the shorter second write keeps the first one's tail

stderr-first-into-dup.reason: > f 2>&1: just-bash collects the command's stdout, then appends its stderr; bash writes both in order through one descriptor

amp-gt.reason: &> f is > f 2>&1: the same stdout-then-stderr order

append-then-dup.reason: >> f 2>&1: the same stdout-then-stderr order, appended

d8-before-after.reason: D8: the shell host runs each invocation as { SCRIPT\n}. A file system error at a redirection then ends the innermost enclosing group, subshell or function body with status 1 (the host's group, if none is nearer): output already produced is kept, the error's path and reason are on stderr, and the rest of that block is skipped, recovery branches (||, if/else) included. GNU bash prints the error, sets status 1 for that command alone and goes on. the output before the failure is kept; 'after' is skipped
